title: Polymer-polymer interdiffusion: effects of entanglements and a polymeric source
abstract: Many industrial applications and biological scenarios involve the interdiffusion of two polymeric species. Motivated by biological subcellular source-driven processes, we study polymer-polymer interdiffusion problems in the absence or the presence of a polymeric source, for both unentangled and entangled scenarios. Utilizing a two-fluid formalism, we arrive at scaling relations, self-similar reductions, and analytical solutions, which are confirmed with one- and two-dimensional numerical simulations. The introduction of a source term breaks the self-similar structure, modifying the boundary conditions and the domain of integration. Nevertheless, we show that the front characteristics of the diffusing droplet exhibit similar spatial structures as in the absence of a source. Our results allow deeper understanding of polymer-polymer interdiffusion and nonlinear transport, especially in the presence of a source.
summary: This paper theoretically models how two different types of polymers diffuse into each other, considering the physical impact of chain entanglements. By using advanced continuum mechanics and nonlinear diffusion equations, the authors show that even when an external source drives the process, the local structure of the diffusing front remains predictable based on established scaling laws.
main_problem: The study investigates polymer-polymer interdiffusion, specifically analyzing how chain entanglements and external polymeric sources affect the transport dynamics.
main_result: The front characteristics of diffusing droplets remain structurally similar whether diffusion is passive or source-driven, although the time evolution scaling exponents change based on entanglement effects.
method: The authors utilize a two-fluid formalism, deriving nonlinear diffusion equations and employing self-similar solutions and asymptotic expansions to solve for concentration profiles in 1D and 2D.
model_or_system: The system models the interdiffusion of two polymeric species (A-mers and B-mers) governed by continuity and momentum conservation equations. The complexity is captured by incorporating entanglement effects via a friction function $\mu(\phi)$ and analyzing regimes ranging from unentangled to highly entangled.
key_observables: Volume fraction profile ($\phi$), droplet radii ($\ell_{in}, \ell_{out}$), mean velocity ($v$), and relative speed ($w$).
important_parameters: Entanglement parameter ($\alpha$), nonlinearity exponent ($m=2$ for unentangled, $m=3$ for entangled), and source term time dependence ($f \propto t^{q-1}$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include neglecting material stresses ($\sigma$) and assuming the system is dominated by osmotic pressure. The analysis also relies on specific power-law forms for the external source.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical and analytical solutions for 1D and 2D interdiffusion, comparing passive vs. source-driven scenarios across unentangled ($\alpha=1$) and entangled ($\alpha\gg 1$) regimes, showing scaling collapse.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general two-fluid formalism to reduced 1D equations of motion. It then analyzes self-similar solutions for passive diffusion, extends this analysis to include an external source term $S$, and finally derives asymptotic forms confirming local geometric similarity despite global changes in scaling.
why_interesting: While focused on polymer physics, the mathematical techniques—deriving nonlinear PDEs from continuum mechanics, using self-similarity reduction, and analyzing non-equilibrium transport far from equilibrium—are highly relevant to modeling complex dynamics in open quantum systems or reaction-diffusion processes in quantum materials.
